premise.claim: PR title: 'optim(utils): sanitize and clamp subpaths to handle path escaping'; commit message: 'prevent escaping mount roots'. The PR body is an unfilled template, so the claim is taken from the title/commit.
premise.reportedComponent: not stated (no linked issue; 'fixes #XXXX' placeholder left in the body)
premise.evidence: On base 05f06659 an untrusted fluid_sub_path of '../../../../../hostonly' makes NodePublishVolume publish a mount source resolving outside the FUSE root; the pod reads 'HOST-ONLY-CONTENT'. On PR head the same input is clamped and the pod reads 'DATASET-CONTENT'. See results/L1_plugins_BASE.txt vs results/L1_plugins_head.txt.

findings.summary: mutator_default.go:337 feeds the sub path into a `bash -c` string built with fmt.Sprintf (check_fuse_default.go:132). CleanSubPath collapses '..' but preserves shell metacharacters, so the postStart hook executes attacker-supplied commands.

The shipped sidecar script's sub path gate is `while [ ! -e  $ConditionPathIsMountPoint/*/$SubPath ]` - unquoted and containing a glob. A sub path with a space makes `[` return 2, so the loop is skipped and the script exits 0, reporting a missing sub path as present. csi/shell/check_mount.sh:48 was already hardened; the two copies have diverged.
Harness-bites guard for F2: an ordinary missing sub path must still be reported missing (exit 2). Proves the gate works normally and is defeated only by the crafted value.

Upgrade regression. An already-persisted absolute fluid_sub_path (reachable on base via `dataset://ns/ds//sub-c`, whose SplitAfterN parse yields '/sub-c') mounted fine before and is now rejected with InvalidArgument. referencedataset/volume.go sets the PV attribute only at creation time, so upgrading the CSI plugin does not rewrite existing values.

CleanSubPath's doc comment claims the result 'can never escape the directory it is later joined to'. filepath.Join/Clean are lexical and do not consider symlinks, so a symlink component still escapes. The code is reasonable; the stated guarantee is not.

No NodePublishVolume coverage for the new validation/clamping. nodeserver_test.go:278-294 discards both the response and the error (`_ = resp; _ = err`), so it passes whether or not absolute paths are rejected and whether or not '../' is clamped. Verified by inspection plus the fact that F3 (a real regression at exactly that call site) ships with all CI green and codecov reporting 50% patch coverage on nodeserver.go.

notVerifiedByTest.summary: Policy inconsistency, a design point rather than a runtime claim: an absolute sub path is rejected at the CSI layer but silently clamped at the other three call sites, and traversal is silently clamped everywhere. `dataset://ns/ds/../../../etc` becomes 'etc' with no error and no log, so the user silently mounts a different directory than they asked for.

Tenant reachability of P0 was established by code reading, not by a live cluster run: GetPhysicalDatasetSubPath (the only producer of the PV attribute) applies no character or traversal validation, Dataset spec.mounts[].mountPoint carries only MinLength=5, and there is no validating webhook on Dataset. Stated at that confidence deliberately.

liveNote: No live layer was needed: the symlink publish method (common.NodePublishMethod=symlink) makes the computed mount source directly observable via os.Readlink, and AnnotationSkipCheckMountReadyTarget=MountPod routes past the check_mount.sh helper that only exists in the CSI image. A live cluster run would additionally confirm the end-to-end tenant path (Dataset -> PV attribute -> pod), which is currently asserted from code reading only (see F7).
